so reviewers immediately see the prior touch count and last touching
checkpoint, even for files outside their immediate familiarity.

Credentials are never read or written by this command — auth is
owned entirely by the user's gh install. Files are sorted by hotspot
score descending so the riskiest pieces float to the top of the
brief. --max-files defaults to 50.

path with cache-backed hotspot annotations, the no-cache hint, and a

understand: prime command (default + --exec for claude-code)

Adds `entire understand prime [<path>...]` — explicit, never-automatic
priming for the next agent session.

Default mode prints (or emits as JSON) a bounded packet:
- Targets section: each target resolved to its node, last touching
  checkpoint, and up to 3 "often co-touched with" notes drawn from the
  shared-checkpoint heuristic the impact command already uses.
- Hotspots section: top-N (default 8) most-touched files inlined so the
  agent has a global picture without needing to call out to other
  understand commands.

- claude-code: looked up via primeBinaryLookup (pluggable for tests),
  packet rendered as markdown and piped on stdin while stdout/stderr go
  to the user's terminal so the agent runs interactively. The lookup +
  runner are package-level vars so tests exercise the full --exec
  composition path without spawning a real CLI.
- any other agent name: clean "not yet supported for --exec; use the
  default packet output and pipe it manually" message — never silently
  exec'd, never falls back to printing the packet, per spec.
- missing --agent flag: explicit error.

Tests cover default markdown output, JSON schema with target +
checkpoint + hotspot fields, missing-agent error, unsupported-agent
message, claude-code happy path with stub lookup/runner, and the
no-cache hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Commands:

  dashboard   Launch the loopback dashboard for the understand graph

  explain     Explain a file or graph node and surface its checkpoint trail
  hotspots    Rank files by checkpoint churn and agent diversity
  impact      Estimate the structural and historical blast radius of a change

Adds `entire understand dashboard` and `entire understand replay`.

Dashboard server (cmd/entire/cli/understand/dashboard/):
- Loopback-only listener via (*net.ListenConfig).Listen on 127.0.0.1:0.
- Per-launch random bearer token (16 bytes via crypto/rand). Token is
  required on every API request via the Authorization header — never
  via query string. Bootstrap injects the token into a script tag so
  the SPA reads it from window state, not from the URL.
- Read-only endpoints:
  /                     embedded HTML shell (vanilla, no node toolchain)
  /api/manifest         build summary
  /api/graph            fused graph (no transcript bodies)
  /api/timeline         replay events
  /api/hotspots         per-file score table
  /api/checkpoint/<id>  reserved for on-demand transcript lookup —
                        returns 404 in v1 to prevent accidental bulk
                        exposure. The route stays registered (and
                        gated by requireToken) so future loaders can't
                        accidentally widen the surface.
- Non-GET methods rejected with 405. Cache-Control: no-store on every
  response. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on JSON and HTML.
- Embedded HTML uses textContent / replaceChildren throughout — no
  innerHTML on user-controlled values. Per-call escaping isn't needed
  because the script never builds HTML strings.

Dashboard CLI (`entire understand dashboard`):
- --print emits the would-bind URL + token without starting the
  listener. Useful for tests and curl-driving the API.
- --open invokes the OS URL opener. The token is never passed to the
  opener — it lives only in the page bootstrap.
- --replay sets a #replay fragment hash so the SPA can default to a
  timeline-first view.

Replay CLI (`entire understand replay`):
- Reads the persisted timeline, sorts by `at` ascending, applies

- Distinct tokens across server instances.
- Live listener URL begins with http://127.0.0.1:.

313	## Configuration
314	
315	Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
316	
317	### settings.json (Project Settings)
318	
319	Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
320	
321	```json
322	{
323	  "enabled": true
324	}
325	```
326	
327	### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
328	
329	Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
330	
331	```json
332	{
333	  "enabled": false,
334	  "log_level": "debug"
335	}
336	```
337	
338	### Configuration Options
339	
340	| Option                               | Values                                       | Description                                             |
341	| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
342	| `enabled`                            | `true`, `false`                              | Enable/disable Entire                                   |
343	| `log_level`                          | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`             | Logging verbosity                                       |
344	| `strategy_options.push_sessions`     | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on git push    |
345	| `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote` | `{"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` | Push checkpoint branches to a separate repo (see below) |
346	| `strategy_options.summarize.enabled` | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-generate AI summaries at commit time               |
347	| `telemetry`                          | `true`, `false`                              | Send anonymous usage statistics to Posthog              |
348	
349	### Agent Hook Configuration
350	
351	Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:
352	
353	| Agent            | Hook Location                 | Format            |
354	| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |

### `.entire/understand/` (Local Cache, Optional)

The `entire understand` command group writes a derived graph + history

build` and contains nothing that can't be rebuilt from the repo plus the

`.gitignore` so the cache stays local:

.entire/understand/

The directory is safe to delete at any time — `entire understand status`

content.text:
All 12 tasks complete, 11 commits landed. Final summary:

**`entire understand` POC — full 8-moment surface delivered**

11 focused commits totaling ~7400 LOC + extensive tests, all lint-clean and test-passing. Each commit is independently reviewable.

**Engine packages** (`cmd/entire/cli/understand/`):
- `graph/` — node/edge/manifest schema + atomic JSON store (7 tests)
- `index/` — repo scan + stdlib `go/parser` symbol extraction; non-Go = file-level (5 tests)
- `history/` — pure CommittedInfo→graph fuser, ScopeFileOwner only with TODO for symbol scope (5 tests)
- `semantic/` — TextGenerator wrapper with 30s timeout, retry-once + degrade, concurrency cap, DataBlock sanitization (12 tests)
- `dashboard/` — loopback HTTP server, per-launch bearer token, header-only auth, embedded vanilla HTML, transcript bulk-leak guard (10 tests)

**CLI commands** (all 11 surfaces, every command ships text + `--json`):
`status`, `build`, `explain`, `tour`, `impact`, `examples`, `hotspots`, `pr`, `prime`, `dashboard`, `replay`.

**Verification:**
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — 0 issues
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/understand/...` — 4/4 packages passing
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/` — all understand command tests passing
- `mise run test:integration` — understand E2E (build→status→explain→hotspots→replay→dashboard) passing
- `mise run test:e2e:canary` — 4/4 Vogon tests passing (no regressions)

**Spec compliance highlights:**
- No new Go module deps; stdlib + existing repo deps only
- No node toolchain; vanilla HTML/CSS/JS via `go:embed`
- Provider resolution reuses summary-generation path; `--provider`/`--model` are per-invocation only (no persistence)
- ScopeFileOwner vs ScopeSymbol never conflated in rendered output
- Dashboard token never in URL/query string; `/api/checkpoint/<id>` returns 404 in v1 to prevent bulk transcript exposure
- `prime --exec` ships claude-code only; other agents get clear "not yet supported" message
- `pr` defers all auth to user's `gh` install
- Build is explicit; no hooks anywhere

**Not pushed.** Branch is `collab/95042499/claude` ready for review.
